title: RT-DETRv2: Improved Baseline with Bag-of-Freebies for Real-Time Detection Transformer

problem.summary: RT-DETRv2 targets three weaknesses of RT-DETR: deformable attention forces the same sampling-point budget on every feature scale, the RT-DETR-specific grid_sample operator constrains deployment, and all scaled detector variants share optimizer hyperparameters that fit them sub-optimally.
statements: The RT-DETR decoder defines the same number of sampling points at each scale, ignoring intrinsic differences between feature scales.
The grid_sample operator specific to RT-DETR limits deployment on hardware where other operators are supported.
Scaled RT-DETR models of different sizes are trained with the same optimizer hyperparameters, resulting in sub-optimal performance.
Strong data augmentation applied throughout training hurts early-stage generalization of the detector.

evidence.quote: We argue that this constraint ignores the intrinsic differences in features at different scales and limits the feature extraction capability of the deformable attention module.
where the RT-DETR-specific grid_sample operator limits its broad applicability.
We also observe that the scaled RT-DETRs of different sizes are trained with the same optimizer hyperparameters, resulting in their sub-optimal performance.

background.summary: The report extends the authors' RT-DETR, which broke real-time detection's dependence on YOLO with an efficient hybrid encoder and uncertainty-minimal query selection, and it builds on DETR and Deformable DETR's sampling-based attention.

relatedWork.quote: The advent of RT-DETR (Zhao et al. [2024]) opens up a new technological avenue for real-time object detection, breaking the dependency on the YOLO in this field.

relatedWork.name: DETR

relatedWork.quote: RT-DETR proposes an efficient hybrid encoder to replace the vanilla Transformer encoder in DETR (Carion et al. [2020]), which significantly improves the inference speed by decoupling the intra-scale interaction and cross-scale fusion of multi-scale features.

relatedWork.name: Deformable DETR
relatedWork.relation: source of the deformable attention module used by the decoder
relatedWork.quote: Current DETRs utilize the deformable attention module (Zhu et al. [2020]) to alleviate the high computational overhead caused by the long sequence of inputs composed of multi-scale features.

evidence.quote: The framework of RT-DETRv2 remains the same as RT-DETR, with only modifications to the deformable attention module of the decoder.
Moreover, RT-DETR provides a wide range of detector sizes and supports flexible speed tuning to accommodate various real-time scenarios without retraining.

solution.summary: Keeping the RT-DETR framework intact, the paper adds bag-of-freebies: per-scale sampling-point counts in deformable attention, an optional rounding-based discrete sampling operator that replaces grid_sample for deployment, dynamic data augmentation that is annealed off near the end of training, and scale-adaptive learning rates for different detector sizes.
solution.approach: Relax RT-DETR's uniform per-scale sampling budget, replace grid_sample with a non-differentiable discrete sampling operator for deployment, and tune augmentation and learning rates per model scale.
components: distinct number of sampling points for each feature scale in deformable attention
optional discrete_sample operator (rounding of predicted sampling offsets) instead of grid_sample
dynamic data augmentation turned off in the last two epochs
scale-adaptive hyperparameter customization (higher lr backbone for small models, lower for large)

evidence.quote: Therefore, we propose to set distinct numbers of sampling points for different scales to achieve more flexible and efficient feature extraction.
Therefore, we propose an optional discrete_sample operator to replace the grid_sample, thus removing the deployment constraints of RT-DETR.
we propose dynamic data augmentation and scale-adaptive hyperparameters customization to improve performance without loss of speed.
we maintain the RT-DETR data augmentation in the early period, while turning off RandomPhotometricDistort, RandomZoomOut, RandomIoUCrop, and MultiScaleInput in the last two epochs.

experiments.summary: RT-DETRv2-S/M/L/X (ResNet18/34/50/101) are trained on COCO train2017 and validated on COCO val2017, compared with RT-DETR at matching scales in AP, AP50 and T4 FPS, with ablations on sampling-point count and on discrete versus grid sampling.

evidence.quote: RT-DETRv2 outperforms RT-DETR at different scales of detectors without loss of speed.
The results show that reducing the number of sampling points does not cause a significant degradation in the performance,

limitations.summary: No limitations section is given; evident constraints are that evaluation covers only COCO with ResNet backbones, discrete sampling needs a non-differentiable workaround plus a separate fine-tuning stage, and it costs a small amount of AP while the largest variant gains nothing over RT-DETR.
items: Experiments are restricted to COCO with ResNet backbones.
The rounding operation used by discrete sampling is non-differentiable, so gradients of the offset predictor must be turned off and a separate fine-tuning stage is required.
Discrete sampling slightly reduces accuracy (47.4 vs 47.9 AP for the S model with grid_sample).
The largest variant shows no improvement over RT-DETR (54.3 AP, +0.0).

evidence.quote: However, the rounding operation is non-differentiable, so we turn off the gradient of the parameters used to predict the sampling offsets.
RT-DETRv2 is trained on COCO (Lin et al. [2014]) train2017 and validated on COCO val2017 dataset.
